summary: This document defines extensions to the iCalendar VALARM component to enhance the use of alarms and improve interoperability between clients and servers. It updates RFC 5545.

eli5.summary: Calendar reminders sometimes behave differently on different apps. This document adds new options to reminder alarms so apps and servers handle them more alike.

questions: how does snoozing work in icalendar
what is the icalendar proximity property
subtitle: Standard ways to identify, acknowledge, snooze and location-trigger iCalendar alarms across clients and servers.

tldr.problem: Calendar alarms (VALARM) had no standard way to say they were dismissed or snoozed, so each client used its own X- properties and alarms on several devices could not stay in sync.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9074 adds a UID and RELATED-TO to alarms, an ACKNOWLEDGED property, a SNOOZE relationship type with a defined snooze procedure, and a PROXIMITY property for location-based triggers.
tldr.outcome: Clients and servers can dismiss an alarm everywhere at once and snooze it interoperably. The RFC also warns that proximity alarms can leak a user's location.

today: RFC 9074 is a Proposed Standard from August 2021 that updates RFC 5545. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its proximity alarms depend on the VLOCATION component from RFC 9073.

sections.title: The Problem with Alarms
sections.content:
iCalendar (RFC 5545) defines the VALARM component, a reminder inside a VEVENT or VTODO. As protocols such as CalDAV (RFC 4791) spread, an event with an alarm often exists on several clients plus the server.

Clients needed a way to show that an alarm was dismissed or snoozed. Until now this was done with custom X- properties specific to each client, which gave poor interoperability. RFC 9074 defines a set of extensions, each in its own section. For the most part each can be supported independently, though some need another. It updates RFC 5545.
sections.eli5: Every reminder app had its own secret way of saying 'snoozed' or 'done'. This document picks one shared way.

sections.title: A More Extensible VALARM
sections.content:
The original VALARM syntax is hard to extend, for example by adding a property common to every kind of alarm. RFC 9074 therefore redefines the base syntax in an alternative form: a VALARM holds properties plus optional subcomponents.

Every alarm still needs ACTION and TRIGGER (once each) plus the property set for its action: audio, display or email. For all three, DURATION and REPEAT are optional but must appear together. Nested subcomponents are new and are needed for proximity triggers.
sections.eli5: The old alarm form was a closed box. The new one has room to add more labels and little boxes inside.

sections.title: Alarm UID and Related To
sections.content:
A UID property may now appear once in a VALARM. It follows RFC 5545 with the security and privacy updates of RFC 7986: it MUST be globally unique and MUST NOT contain security- or privacy-sensitive information.

With a UID, alarms can refer to one another. The RELATED-TO property is now allowed in alarms, and specific relationship kinds are expressed by registering new RELTYPE values. This is what makes snoozing possible.
sections.eli5: Each alarm gets a name tag so other alarms can say 'I am the follow-up to that one'.

sections.title: Acknowledging Alarms
sections.content:
If every device performs an alarm when it fires, a user gets several alerts and wants to dismiss one and have the rest follow. For recurring events, clients also need to know the last time an alarm was acknowledged, to spot missed ones.

The new ACKNOWLEDGED property holds the UTC date-time when the alarm was last sent or acknowledged, for example ACKNOWLEDGED:20090604T084500Z. Clients SHOULD set it to the current UTC time when the user acknowledges a pending alarm. For alarms where feedback is not possible, such as email, they SHOULD set it when the alarm triggers and the action succeeds.

  • If it is present and greater than or equal to the computed trigger time, a client SHOULD NOT trigger the alarm.
  • If it appears or changes while an alert is showing and is at least the trigger time, clients SHOULD dismiss the alert.
sections.eli5: When you tap 'done' on one device, it writes the time on the alarm. The other devices see the note and stop ringing.

sections.title: Snoozing
sections.content:
The RFC defines a standard snooze. To snooze a triggered alarm, a client MUST:

  1. Set ACKNOWLEDGED on the triggered alarm.
  2. Create a new snooze alarm as a sibling in the same parent component. It MUST trigger at the chosen interval after the original fired (clients SHOULD use an absolute UTC TRIGGER). It MUST carry a RELATED-TO with RELTYPE=SNOOZE whose value is the original alarm's UID; the client MUST add a UID to the original if it has none.
  3. When the snooze alarm fires, update ACKNOWLEDGED on the original. If snoozed again, remove that snooze alarm and repeat step 2. If dismissed, either set ACKNOWLEDGED on it or remove it.

Apart from ACKNOWLEDGED, the original alarm is left unchanged. The SNOOZE relationship type is registered for this purpose. In the RFC's example, a 15-minute-before alarm is snoozed for 5 minutes, snoozed again for 5 minutes, then dismissed.
sections.eli5: Pressing snooze does not change your first alarm. The phone makes a fresh little alarm that says 'I belong to that one' and rings again soon.

sections.title: Proximity Triggers
sections.content:
Alarms can also fire based on place. The PROXIMITY property says a location-based trigger is used and which action fires it. Its values are:

  • ARRIVE and DEPART: the calendar user agent arrives in, or leaves, the vicinity of one or more locations. Each location MUST be given as a VLOCATION component (from RFC 9073) with a URL holding a 'geo' URI. 'Vicinity' is implementation defined.
  • CONNECT and DISCONNECT: the agent connects to, or disconnects from, an automobile paired via Bluetooth. There is no way to target a particular automobile.

TRIGGER is still required for backwards compatibility, but with a proximity alarm it has to be ignored. Clients SHOULD use a value far in the past, and 19760401T005545Z has commonly been used. VLOCATION subcomponents are allowed only when PROXIMITY is present.
sections.eli5: Instead of 'remind me at 5 o'clock', you can say 'remind me when I leave the office'. The phone watches where you are.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
An alarm that is not monitored can annoy users or leak information. An audio alert could embarrass, and an email alert could leak a location to a third party or send unsolicited mail to many users. So CalDAV clients and servers that accept iCalendar data from a third party (for example via iTIP, a subscription feed or a shared calendar) SHOULD remove each VALARM before storing it.

A proximity alarm stored on a shared CalDAV calendar reveals when a user intends to arrive at or leave a place. If a client then writes ACKNOWLEDGED back, it leaks the exact time they did. Clients that implement proximity alarms SHOULD let users keep the alarm and its acknowledgement on the local device only.
sections.eli5: Do not let strangers put alarms in your calendar, and be careful sharing alarms that reveal where you are going.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC adds two properties, ACKNOWLEDGED and PROXIMITY, to the iCalendar Properties registry, and the SNOOZE value to the Relationship Types registry. It also creates a new registry of PROXIMITY values, initialised with ARRIVE, DEPART, CONNECT and DISCONNECT. More values may be registered using the process in Section 8.2.1 of RFC 5545.
sections.eli5: The new words are added to the official list so everyone spells them the same way.

messages.label: Set ACKNOWLEDGED
messages.note: The user chose to snooze the triggered alarm.

messages.label: Create sibling alarm
messages.note: Absolute UTC TRIGGER and RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=SNOOZE pointing at the original UID.

messages.label: Update ACKNOWLEDGED
messages.note: If snoozed again, remove the snooze alarm and create a new one; if dismissed, acknowledge or remove it.

items.label: Arrive
items.desc: Fires on arriving in the vicinity of the VLOCATION(s).

items.label: Depart
items.desc: Fires on leaving the vicinity of the VLOCATION(s).

items.label: Connect
items.desc: Fires on connecting to a Bluetooth-paired automobile.

items.label: Disconnect
items.desc: Fires on disconnecting from a Bluetooth-paired automobile.

data.title: Remind when leaving the office
data.code:
BEGIN:VALARM
UID:77D80D14-906B-4257-963F-85B1E734DBB6
ACTION:DISPLAY
TRIGGER;VALUE=DATE-TIME:19760401T005545Z
DESCRIPTION:Remember to buy milk
PROXIMITY:DEPART
BEGIN:VLOCATION
UID:123456-abcdef-98765432
NAME:Office
URL:geo:40.443,-79.945;u=10
END:VLOCATION
END:VALARM
